nodes.label: Classification Gap
nodes.rationale: Models produce inaccurate hallucination labels under zero-shot prompting; structured prompts and explicit reasoning partially close this gap in HRLs but not LRLs, motivating the paper's five-strategy comparison.

nodes.label: Prompting Cannot Fully Fix Multilingual Limitations
nodes.rationale: All prompting strategies (few-shot, CoT, CoTR, multi-agent) show reduced or inconsistent gains on low-resource languages, implying prompting alone cannot address underlying multilingual model limitations even though it partially closes the classification gap for high-resource languages.

nodes.author: Andrew Bernas, Minoo Kim, Samantha Liu, Winston Liu, Shivani Sahni, Kaishuu Shinozaki-Conefrey, Dhruv Shrivastava, Anahita Srinivasan, Alexandra Chin, Erik Luna, Alan Yu, Pulkit Tandon

nodes.label: VOC Sensor Array (MQ-3, MQ-136, MQ-137, MQ-138)
nodes.norm_label: voc sensor array (mq-3, mq-136, mq-137, mq-138)

nodes.label: Single-Sensor Nearest-Neighbor Identification
nodes.rationale: PCA clustering with all sensors proved unreliable because most sensors varied more with recording time/environment than with smell identity; the team observed only the alcohol sensor had low deviation for a given smell, so they switched to nearest-neighbor classification on that single sensor's readings, which ultimately gave the most accurate real-world results despite lower theoretical sophistication.

nodes.label: Mist Maker Synthesis Design Choice
nodes.rationale: Considered spray bottle, pressurized canister, solid-state smells, and mist maker; chose mist maker (piezoelectric ultrasonic vaporizer) because it used simple, readily-available parts and avoided the servo-torque and pressure-chamber engineering problems of the alternatives, and avoided the heat requirement of solid scents.
